text: It's, um, I was, I was actually in Silverstone for, I think it was Friday practice, and I went back to Finland and, uh, on Sunday morning, and, uh, I saw Michael's accident on the TV in the airport. And, uh, I didn't think much of it and, uh, because it didn't look big, so I, I was just hoping he's fine. And, uh, then a couple hours later I heard he broke his leg and, uh, didn't think anything. So, uh, I was getting married during the next week. We had a, like, a wedding rehearsal on Monday, and then I had a phone call from Jean Todt. Aye, yai, yai. And, uh, he called me when we were practicing this wedding and, uh, and, um, he said, uh, "I want you to come to Maranello." And I thought, "Oh, okay." Uh, I- of course immediately I can connect these two things and, uh, he, uh... I asked, "When?" He said, "Now." So he did not give me option. I said, "I'm my wed- I'm in my wedding re- rehearsal." And he said, "It doesn't matter. You come to Maranello now." Two hours later I was in airplane. So, uh, to take the wheel of the car for Michael Schumacher is not easy because it is a- he had all his crew behind him. Uh, it was a particular moment, I think a, a difficult moment for you to, to, to adapt at, at his style of, of driving, for example? Yeah, it was... Ferrari was very kind to me when I went there. It was, I felt very welcome from day one. We had a really good time of staying in Jean's house in Maranello, and, uh, Jean, Jean is like a workaholic. He works non-stop. Uh, he sleeps, like, two hours a night, and then he works all the other time, so I never saw him. And, uh, I was getting very hungry in his house because there was no food, so, uh, Ross Brawn brought me some food in the evening to eat and, uh, but, uh, I felt so welcomed from beginning. And, uh, every time I went to factory and everybody was helping me, and I had phone calls with Michael also, and Michael helped me how to adapt in the team quickly. Quickly and because next race was already one week later. So he was supportive on this time to, to help you to find- Yes ... the best way to adapt to the car. I, I talked a lot with Michael on the phone and, uh, we had video calls and, uh, and, uh, he was helping me a lot, um, to teach me about the people in team, who I need to go if I need something specific for the car. So he told me the names which are who I need to talk and, uh, it just, uh, it, it was very, very easy to adapt. And of course I knew Eddie from before also, so it was quite easy, easy to get help from him also. And you, you were quickly competitive because some, uh, weeks a- after that in Germany you are close to, to win. Yes. Um, first race was Austria and, uh, it was sort of okay, but, uh, I did got no testing at all straight there. And then after Austria we came here to Mugello for I think three days. I drove non-stop from morning. We could play a little bit with the car and it was more comfortable for me, and then in Germany I could have won it. And it was a particular moment for you because, uh, you, you were in ahead and close to win, and you have a call on the radio. I don't know if it was Ross Brawn or Jean Todt- Yes ... who asked you to let Eddie Irvine to, to win because he was, uh, uh, fighting for the championship. Mm. I presume it was a very, uh, tough moment for you. Yeah, but we, we talked about this, uh, before my first race. Uh, Jean gave me, like, a two-hour lesson how important it is that I help team and Eddie only to win the championship because I have no chance to win. So, uh, if this situation comes up that Eddie is behind me, I need to let him pass. And so I knew of course the whole Hockenheim race when I was leading, I had, uh, Heinz-Harald Frentzen behind me. I s- it was yellow car. I was all the time hoping, "Yes, stay there. Stay there." And then Eddie managed to pass Heinz during pit stops, and then I saw red car behind me and I thought, "Oh, okay, and now I know what's gonna happen next." And then very soon came the radio call from Ross Brawn with his calm voice that, "Mika, I want you to let Eddie pass this lap." Yeah. And you sacrificed your- [coughs] Excuse me. And you f- sacrificed your first victory for, for the, the happiness of the Scuderia and of- also for the giving the maximum chance for Eddie Irvine. Uh, uh, you have a, a special relationship with, uh, with, uh, Michael Schumacher on this time. We, um, like a fan, we, uh, we have the vision of a, a driver who is very, uh, implicated in, uh, very serious in, in his jobs. And all people we met today in Mugello said he, he was a, a so kind driver, a so kind a gentleman in the life. Yeah, he was nice guy. We, we knew each other from karting already, and we used to race karting. We did, uh, Formula Ford together. Actually, I beat him in Formula Ford quite, mm, I fin- won the European Championship, but Michael finished second. And, uh, Formula 3 we were, uh, Macau Grand Prix, Michael won, I was second, and Eddie third. [laughs] So it's, we, we've been, we've been growing up- It's a long story between you and him ... we've been growing up together, so I know him from a long time. Yeah. And after this, uh, experience you have a, um, a vision different of Formula One because it was maybe the, the most important, uh, uh, team, uh, for who you drive on this time. I know you, you have experiences with, uh, with, uh, Toyota, you experiences with other crew. Uh, but it was a different strategy, different organization. It's a big, big factory. It's really a, a different culture, DNA in the Ferrari. Yeah, it was my first, like, big team. I was in Tyrrell and Arrows and, uh, smaller teams before, so it was first, like, a big team and, uh, of course it opened my eyes for many things. Uh, how quick they can react for if you need something for the car and, uh, they would do it immediately, not think about it for two weeks, and, uh, it was in the car immediately. And the factory was working non-stop and, uh, the resources they have, and we were testing so much. We had a different test team waiting every time after the race. We went to s- different circuits and there was a test team waiting and, uh- So many laps and so much testing. Sometimes I got the call in the middle of the night in Maranello and some engineer found something in the dampers. So I went to the middle of the night, they woke me up and come here. I went there and did three laps over the curbs and then go back to sleep. This track here in Mugello has a particular importance in the success of the Scuderia this time because to have a private practice track, it was an element key for victory. Yeah, we did a lot of laps here in Mugello and it's a very challenging track for the car setup wise. And there's every type of corners. There's high speed corners and there's some bumps and you get everything working here really well. If the car works here, it will work everywhere. And this experience for Ferrari, I believe was wonderful for you because it gave you a great exposition, worldwide exposition with your amazing results. It was a chance for you to go to Toyota behind. It's Ferrari who gave you this opportunity to go to Toyota? Yeah, sort of. I went to Sauber first because they had a Ferrari engine. So John wanted to put me in Sauber to stay in the family, kind of. But then Toyota came up after that and Toyota was like my chance to get in another big team. Only problem, Toyota had Ange Pasquale. He was the only problem with the Toyota. No, it's a joke. Yeah, I know. We say hello to Ange. So thank you, Mika, for this interview. And I hope we can make a big show with you when you have a moment with us. Thank you very much. Bye-bye. Thank you.
